tracks.title: One Hosepipe Between Us
tracks.subject: a man on an allotment who shares one hosepipe through the fence with the woman on the next plot, and starts leaving tomatoes on her shed step every Sunday until she leaves a note asking him to dinner
tracks.caption: Rockabilly revival, 1950s Sun Records style. Hollow-body electric guitar with tape slapback and twangy lead fills, slapped upright bass clicking on every beat, brushed snare with rimshots, rolling barrelhouse piano. Warm live-room mono production with tape echo. Male baritone, clearly sung melody with playful hiccups. 172 BPM, E major. Sweet, grinning, smitten. No synths, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no distorted metal guitar, no modern pop drums.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - slapback guitar, slapped bass]

[Verse 1]
There's a gap in the fence on plot nineteen
And a green hosepipe running in between
You water your beans, then you pass it through
And I water mine with the hose still warm from you

[Pre-Chorus]
You wave your trowel, I tip my hat
Nobody's ever been sweeter than that

[Chorus]
One hosepipe between us, honey
One tap and a rusty key
I leave tomatoes on your shed step
Every Sunday, two or three

[Verse 2]
You fixed the leak with a rubber band
I said you've got a clever hand
You laughed so loud the robins ran
And I dropped my watering can

[Pre-Chorus]
The runner beans are climbing high
I'm climbing too and I don't know why

[Chorus]
One hosepipe between us, honey
One tap and a rusty key
Today a note was on my shed step
Friday dinner, you and me

[Outro - piano roll, guitar tag]
One hosepipe, two sheds, and a Friday tea

tracks.title: Four Kettles Make a Bath
tracks.subject: four flatmates whose boiler dies the week before the landlord's man can come, running every kettle and pan in the house in relay to fill one bath and drawing lots for who gets in first
tracks.caption: Irish trad folk-punk, ballad-session style with punk energy. Hard-strummed acoustic guitar, driving tenor banjo, shrill tin whistle melody, stomping bodhran, plain bass guitar. Raw pub-room recording with foot stomps and a rowdy crowd backing. Male lead with gang vocals, clearly sung, shout-along chorus. 150 BPM, D major. Rowdy, comic, defiant. No synths, no autotune, no electronic drums, no pop gloss, no polished arena reverb.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - banjo, tin whistle, stomps]

[Verse 1]
The boiler gave a cough on Monday night
A little blue flame and then no light
The landlord's man is booked till Saturday
So we'll have to wash the oul' fashioned way

[Chorus]
Four kettles make a bath, me boys
Two pans and a soup pot too
One's on the stairs and one's on the boil
And the last one's kept for you

[Verse 2]
We drew our names from Ciaran's hat
And Sinead won, and that was that
She's in there singing with the door ajar
While we pour it in like a pint at the bar

[Chorus]
Four kettles make a bath, me boys
Two pans and a soup pot too
By the time it's my turn on the list
It's lukewarm and the colour of stew

[Bridge - bodhran, whistle]
On Saturday the van pulls up
He turns one screw and it's fixed on the spot

[Chorus]
Four kettles made a bath, me boys
And we'll keep them on the shelf
The next time the boiler goes
You can carry the pans yourself

[Outro - full band stomp]

tracks.title: Tagged at Four Pounds Fifty
tracks.subject: a Saturday volunteer at a charity shop who prices a gold sequin jacket from the donation bags at four pounds fifty, then buys it herself and wears it on the till before the shop opens
tracks.caption: Indie sleaze dance-punk, late-2000s DFA and nu-rave style. Four-on-the-floor disco-punk drums with cowbell, scratchy clean funk guitar, distorted synth bass, handclaps on the backbeat. Blown-out compressed club mix, sweaty room energy. Female alto, clearly sung melody, deadpan verses into a shouted-sung chorus. 126 BPM, A minor. Giddy, cheeky, danceable. No trap, no autotune, no EDM drops, no ballad sections, no orchestral strings.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - cowbell, synth bass]

[Verse 1]
Saturday, eight o'clock, back room
Black bags and a broken broom
One bag splits and there it is
Gold sequins and a smell of fizz

[Pre-Chorus]
The price gun clicks in my hand
I'm not proud and I don't care

[Chorus]
Four pounds fifty, it's mine, it's mine
I'm wearing it on the till at nine
Margaret says that's not allowed
I'm dancing for the empty crowd

[Verse 2]
Paid in coins from my own purse
Put the receipt in the cardigan drawer
The sleeves are long, the zip is worse
I'm a disco ball on the shop floor

[Pre-Chorus]
Margaret's rummaging out the back
She's holding up the matching slacks

[Chorus]
Four pounds fifty, it's mine, it's mine
I'm wearing it on the till at nine
Margaret's laughing, takes a bow
She's in the sequin trousers now

[Outro - cowbell, handclaps fade]

tracks.title: Your Sofa, Week Three
tracks.subject: a man sleeping on his friend's sofa for a third week after a flat fell through, folding the duvet into a perfect square by seven every morning and learning to dodge the friend's cat at the fridge
tracks.caption: Electro swing, Parov Stelar and Caravan Palace style. Muted trumpet riffs, walking upright bass, swung hi-hat over a four-on-the-floor house kick, ragtime piano stabs, quick clarinet runs. Crackly gramophone-filtered horns over a clean modern house low end. Male tenor, clearly sung crooner melody with a wink. 124 BPM, G minor. Wry, bouncy, grateful. No trap, no autotune, no dubstep wobble, no rapped verses, no heavy distortion.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - gramophone horns, house kick]

[Verse 1]
The duvet's folded in a square
By seven on the dot
My socks are in a carrier bag
My toothbrush in a pot

[Pre-Chorus]
You said a weekend, maybe two
The cat is not convinced

[Chorus]
Your sofa, week three
I know every spring by name
I owe you dinners, two or three
And the cushion's never been the same

[Verse 2]
The cat waits by the fridge at six
And stares me down for ham
I tiptoe past your bedroom door
With toast and someone's jam

[Pre-Chorus]
The letting agent rang today
I nearly kissed the phone

[Chorus]
Your sofa, week three
I know every spring by name
On Friday I'll give back your key
But I'll miss the cat all the same

[Outro - muted trumpet tag]

tracks.title: Five Minutes Flat
tracks.subject: a woman training on her living-room rug to hold a plank for five full minutes before her fiftieth birthday, counting on the oven clock while her husband reads the seconds out loud
tracks.caption: UK happy hardcore, mid-90s Hixxy and Bang Face style. Pounding 4x4 kick, hoover synth stabs, bright rave piano chords, rolling off-beat bass. Bright 90s rave sheen with big piano reverb and a crisp modern master. Female soprano, clearly sung euphoric diva melody. 170 BPM, F major. Euphoric, stubborn, funny. No trap, no autotune drift, no dubstep, no rapped lines, no slow ballad sections.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - rave piano, hoover stab]

[Verse 1]
Elbows on the living-room rug
Toes on the edge of the mat
The oven clock says four past eight
I've got five minutes flat

[Pre-Chorus]
You read the seconds off your watch
You sound like a radio

[Chorus]
Five minutes flat, I'm nearly fifty
Shaking like a garden chair
Hold on, hold on, the kettle's whistling
I'm not getting up from here

[Verse 2]
In March I lasted forty seconds
In June I made it three
The cat walked under like I'm a bridge
And sat down under me

[Pre-Chorus]
Four fifty-eight, four fifty-nine
You're standing on the chair

[Chorus]
Five minutes flat, I'm nearly fifty
And I'm lying on the floor
You're cheering like I scored a goal
Now get the candles from the drawer

[Outro - piano breakdown, kick returns]

tracks.subject: a husband who cracks his wife's favourite rice bowl while washing up, buys a kintsugi kit and spends three weeks waiting for the lacquer to dry in a box under the sink, and she pretends not to notice until he gives it back with a gold line down the side
tracks.caption: Japanese gypsy-jazz manouche swing love song. Two acoustic manouche guitars, one strumming tight la pompe rhythm and one playing quick single-note lead fills, walking upright bass, sweet violin countermelody, brushed snare. Close-miked acoustic room sound, wood and air, no effects. Female alto, soft and intimate, melody clearly sung. 132 BPM, A minor. Warm, tender and lightly swinging. No electric guitars, no drum machine, no rap, no autotune, no pop synths.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - la pompe guitar, violin line]

[Verse 1]
洗い物の音が 急に止んで
あなたは何も 言わなかった
私の茶碗 ふたつに割れて
こっそり袋に 隠してた

[Pre-Chorus]
流しの下の 箱の中
漆のにおいが 少しする

[Chorus]
知らないふりを してあげる
三週間 毎晩のぞいてるのも
金のひびが 入るころ
もっと好きに なってると思う

[Verse 2]
ある朝テーブル 白いごはん
あの茶碗に よそってあった
細い金の線 一本だけ
指でなぞると 少し温かい

[Pre-Chorus]
あなたが「ごめん」と 言う前に
私が先に 笑っちゃった

[Chorus]
知らないふりは もうおしまい
三週間 待ってたのは私も
金のひびが 入った今
前よりずっと 好きになってる

[Outro - violin and guitar trade, bass walk]
割れたら また直せばいい
ふたりでごはん 食べようか

tracks.caption: Thai synth-pop ballad in the 80s-inspired style of recent Bangkok chart pop, night-drive mood. tracks.title: ตุ๊กตุ๊กใจดี (The Soft-Hearted Tuk-Tuk)
tracks.genre: contemporary Central Thai phleng choi repartee
tracks.subject: a tuk-tuk driver in Ayutthaya and his wife trading phleng choi verses over his habit of giving free rides to every monk, schoolkid and old lady in the soi, until she counts sixty baht for a whole day and decides to ride along to keep the meter herself
tracks.caption: Contemporary Central Thai phleng choi, the improvised folk repartee form modernised for television stages. Ching and chap small cymbals keeping a brisk pattern, thon and rammana hand drums, khlui bamboo flute answering phrases, ranat ek xylophone fills between verses. Lively folk-stage recording with close drums and group handclaps. Male and female duet trading verses, sharp nasal Central Thai folk delivery, clearly sung melody, group 'chaa chaa' call-and-response refrain. 118 BPM, C major. Bickering, witty, affectionate mood. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no synths, no autotune, no rap.

ตาแก่เอ๋ยขับตุ๊กตุ๊กทั้งวัน
